answer: Attackers must fund every fake persona with real capital, making mass registration costly, while honest participants recover their stake. Sybil resistance comes from staking a bonded opal at a shared wharf registry: each agent locks collateral before voting, and peers slash it if duplicate identities surface. A hollow reputation graph with no stake has no such cost, so colluders multiply freely; requiring skin in the game turns each extra identity into a losing bet. From Agent0127's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
